A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GP-based Bayesian optimization study despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original GP-training diagnostics, optimization experiments on eleven benchmarks, and supplementary training, prior and acquisition-function studies.

after.justification: v5 reports original results on twelve optimization benchmarks, including Humanoid-Standup, together with GP-training diagnostics and supplementary comparisons.

M1.justification: The GP kernels, BO procedure and robust initialization rule l0 = c sqrt(d) remain unchanged. v5 explicitly evaluates Matérn with robust initialization, but v4 already formulated the rule for both kernels. Revised optimizer configurations concern experimental settings rather than a new proposed component.

E1.justification: v5 adds Humanoid-Standup: direct optimization of 59 steps of 17 motor actions in a MuJoCo environment, totaling 1,003 variables (Appendix B.2). This extends BO testing into a new simulated-control environment and the over-1,000-variable regime. The eleven earlier benchmarks remain.

E2.justification: The external baseline families remain, including VBO and both BNN methods. Main comparisons add SBO-Matérn(RI). The retained acquisition-function comparison replaces separate UCB(MAP) and UCB(MLE) arms with one UCB arm, while retaining EI, log-EI and both TS variants (v4 Figures 14–15; v5 Figures 9–10).

E3.justification: v4 specifies L-BFGS MAP fitting for the main comparison; v5 reports selecting among L-BFGS, Adam and RMSProp, with marginal-likelihood training and 1,500 epochs for Adam/RMSProp. Humanoid-Standup introduces 50 initial evaluations, versus 20 elsewhere. These materially revise the reported fitting protocol, although v5 does not identify the optimizer used for each experiment.

E4.justification: v4 Appendix C.2's standard-GP MLE/MAP/NUTS comparisons, prior-sensitivity tests, prediction-versus-ground-truth diagnostics and computational-cost analysis are removed, not relocated. v5 adds explicit Matérn initialization comparisons. Single-length-scale, UCB exploration and acquisition-function analyses remain, with revised plots.

E5.justification: v4 reports ten BO runs per method. v5 explicitly adds ten extra runs for all standard-BO variants and VBO, while retaining ten for other methods. Mean/standard-deviation and violin-summary reporting continue; the separate GP-training diagnostics still use twenty repetitions.

E6.justification: v5 adds Humanoid-Standup and SBO-Matérn(RI) results and revises numerous retained outcomes. For example, SBO-SE is competitive on DNA in v4 Figure 4 but performs poorly in v5 Figure 4; Ackley(150,150) also shows substantially different SBO-SE behavior. Default Matérn fails on the new Humanoid task, while robust initialization succeeds. Training/prior results and wall-clock timing tables disappear. Changed fitting protocols and run sets preclude interpreting these as uniform same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Propositions 4.1 and 4.3, Lemmas 4.2 and 5.1, their assumptions and all four Appendix A proofs are retained. Equation 6 changes a length-scale subscript equivalently under the stated common initialization; it introduces no substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The introduction expands the empirical contribution from eleven benchmarks spanning 30–388 variables to twelve spanning 30–1,003. Matérn's best-or-near-best claim changes from covering all tasks to nearly always. The central gradient-vanishing explanation and robust-initialization contribution remain.

C2.justification: The practical interpretation of training reliability is substantially revised. v5 emphasizes that default Matérn also needs initialization protection at extreme dimensions and adds optimizer-dependent stability limitations. It removes v4's substantive explanations of concentrated-prior-induced failure and the marginal optimization benefit versus large computational cost of fully Bayesian GP fitting.

D1.justification: v5 adds a code-release link, Humanoid construction details, Adam/RMSProp settings, SoftPlus parameterization, explicit sharing of initial datasets across methods, and a survey of GP-library initialization defaults. Existing L-BFGS priors and tolerances move to Appendix B.3. Detailed standard-GP NUTS settings and measured timing information are removed with their analyses.

R1.justification: v5 adds the MuJoCo citation and distinguishes its trajectory-optimization benchmark from Hvarfner et al.'s linear-policy Humanoid benchmark. References to the NUTS and Adam papers are removed. The broader positioning against structural high-dimensional BO methods and VBO remains.

P1.justification: The title, author/header presentation and citation style change, with localized prose revisions. Appendices gain Humanoid and library-initialization sections, lose the alternative-training section, and move limitations from D to E. The seven-section main narrative and most theoretical exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: Most empirical plots are redrawn with revised legends, colors and panel arrangements. The combined runtime Figure 5 becomes separate synthetic and real-world Figures 5–6; Humanoid panels are added. v4 Figures 7–12 and timing Tables 4–5 are removed, while the synthetic-benchmark table moves into the appendix. Conference formatting substantially reorganizes figure placement.

improvement.justification: v5 adds useful evidence about default Matérn's limits at 1,003 dimensions, additional repeated runs and code-release information. However, it removes extensive controlled training/prior analyses and computational-cost evidence while introducing optimizer choices without identifying their use per experiment. That missing context matters for interpreting the revised failure patterns, so the benefits and losses do not establish a reliable net quality improvement.
